# Study v3 results: group-aware evaluation (generated by `tools/render_study_v3_doc.py` from `reports/study_v3/`)

Protocol: [STUDY_V3_PROTOCOL](../methodology/STUDY_V3_PROTOCOL.md) (v3.0, frozen before any v3 training). Pre-training review: [STUDY_V3_PHASE2_REVIEW](../methodology/STUDY_V3_PHASE2_REVIEW.md).
Study v2 (commits `c10014f`, `cec8ebd`) is unchanged and remains the historical record. **Groups are image-similarity components, not patient/scan IDs.** Nothing here is confirmatory: the official test set was examined before.

## 1. Reproducibility report
- **Runs:** 53 completed, 0 failed, 1 smoke run (separate tree, never reported): 8 selection runs (fold 0, seed 42: A + 7 B grid points) and 45 final runs (A, B, C x folds 0-4 x seeds 1, 2, 3); plus a descriptive test evaluation of each final model.
- **Frozen artifacts** (`experiments/study_v3/protocol/FROZEN`, frozen 2026-10-16T19:30:22+00:00): group manifest `057775550af464df...` (logical hash `fab04204...5d79` inside the file), fold manifest file sha `f8be20e8dd39af9f...` (logical hash `9c0fe67b...33a5`), protocol, configs and result-producing code (SHA-256 list in the marker). HEAD at freeze `cec8ebd`, working tree dirty (this study's new files; nothing committed).
- **Verification:** `tools/verify_study_v3.py` (independent rebuild of the groups from raw images: identical; zero file and group overlap in all folds; every group evaluated once); 185 tests passed; every run manifest records both manifest hashes; `verify_artifacts` passed for all runs used in the analysis.
- **Environment:** conda env `torch-gpu` (Python 3.10, torch 2.5.1+cu121), RTX 4060 Laptop GPU 8 GB, Windows 11; about 5 minutes per 30-epoch run on about 590 training images. Seeds and cuDNN deterministic mode are set; residual CUDA nondeterminism is possible.
- **Commands:** `python tools/create_study_v3_manifests.py; python tools/verify_study_v3.py; python tools/create_freeze_v3.py;` then `python tools/run_study_v3.py --exp A --fold 0 --seed 42 --purpose selection` and the B grid, `python tools/select_b_v3.py`, the 45 final runs (`--purpose final`), `final_test_v3` for each, `python tools/build_reports_v3.py`, `python tools/render_study_v3_doc.py`.
- **Deviations and process notes (all recorded before results were seen unless stated):** (1) a first fold layout put the 120-image group alone as a validation set; it was replaced by the current rule before the freeze and before any model was trained. (2) After the freeze a convenience flag (`--stage1-only`) was added to `tools/select_b_v3.py` before any run; documented in `FROZEN_ADDENDUM_1.json` (selection logic unchanged). (3) The FROZEN marker's `python` field records the shell interpreter (3.14.4), not the training environment; run manifests record the real environment. (4) The B retrain point was fixed by the declared rule (below), not by results on evaluation groups.

## 2. Grouped-split audit
54 similarity groups (34 x 10, 12 x 20, 1 x 30, 5 x 40, 1 x 70, 1 x 120 images; r > 0.99, 64x64 thumbnails). Zero file and zero group overlap between train / validation / calibration / evaluation in every fold.
Sizes (groups/images): train 26-31 / 580-600, validation 5-9 / 100-120, calibration 6-8 / 100-110, evaluation 8-12 / 200. Held-out images still have training neighbours at median correlation 0.95-0.97 (official test: 0.896; max 0.94), so v3 held-out data are closer to training data than the official test set. Details: `reports/study_v3/phase2_verification.json`.

| C - A | rmse | 0.0560 | [-0.0011, 0.1189] | [-0.0102, 0.1299] | no | 0.144, -0.121, 0.145 |
| C - A | mean_corr | -0.0300 | [-0.0570, -0.0003] | [-0.0618, 0.0028] | no | -0.072, 0.052, -0.070 |

**Reading.** By the declared rule, B is demonstrated better than A at the evaluation-group level on the primary metric and on RMSE, and C is not demonstrated different from A. Three qualifiers apply and must travel with the claim: (1) B's advantage is **not consistent across training seeds** (mean-correlation difference per seed +0.034, +0.017, -0.002) and is about half the seed-to-seed SD of the metric (0.03), which the group bootstrap does not include; (2) B's hyperparameters were chosen on fold-0 validation (8 groups; barely meeting the improvement rule) and share training groups with other folds' evaluation groups, a mild selection effect; (3) groups are not patients and there are at most 54 of them. The result contradicts the null found in v2, where the image-level validation split was optimistic; v3 supports at most a **small, seed-dependent benefit of the ranking objective**, not a robust one. C's per-seed differences with A range from -0.07 to +0.05, i.e. seed-to-seed variability dominates.

## 6. Experiment C: conformal coverage and interval width (target 0.90)
Assumptions (protocol section 7): P (grouped split conformal) needs calibration and evaluation groups exchangeable; calibration is one fold's 6-8 groups, so per-fold coverage is noisy. S (grouped cross-conformal) pools the other four folds' held-out residuals (about 800 images); models differ across folds, so its guarantee is approximate. The quantile was never tuned on evaluation or test coverage.

| Method | Pooled coverage, mean over seeds [95% group-bootstrap] | Covered / 1000 (seeds 1, 2, 3) | Mean width (seeds 1-3) | Median width (seeds 1-3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P grouped split conformal (primary) | 0.919 [0.900, 0.940] | 911/1000, 933/1000, 913/1000 | 1.83, 1.71, 1.83 | 1.69, 1.59, 1.86 |
| S grouped cross-conformal (secondary) | 0.893 [0.862, 0.926] | 895/1000, 894/1000, 891/1000 | 1.84, 1.63, 1.92 | 1.70, 1.41, 1.46 |
| constant-width comparator (P) | 0.916 [0.884, 0.948] | 916/1000, 935/1000, 897/1000 | 1.90, 1.59, 1.72 | 1.47, 1.53, 1.39 |
| constant-width comparator (S) | 0.883 [0.837, 0.921] | 867/1000, 896/1000, 885/1000 | 1.96, 1.42, 1.74 | 2.07, 1.41, 1.80 |

Per-fold covered counts (out of 200 held-out images), P:

| Seed | f0 | f1 | f2 | f3 | f4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 191/200 | 170/200 | 196/200 | 171/200 | 183/200 |
| 2 | 178/200 | 174/200 | 196/200 | 193/200 | 192/200 |
| 3 | 171/200 | 185/200 | 197/200 | 187/200 | 173/200 |

S:

| Seed | f0 | f1 | f2 | f3 | f4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 193/200 | 148/200 | 175/200 | 191/200 | 188/200 |
| 2 | 186/200 | 175/200 | 143/200 | 193/200 | 197/200 |
| 3 | 168/200 | 178/200 | 156/200 | 189/200 | 200/200 |

Uncertainty diagnostics (pooled, held-out groups):

| Seed | Spearman(sigma, abs error) | Gaussian NLL (0-4 scale, no constant) | mean sigma | P coverage by sigma tercile (low, mid, high) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.416 | 0.061 | 0.384 | 0.87, 0.94, 0.92 |
| 2 | 0.146 | -0.311 | 0.421 | 0.93, 0.91, 0.95 |
| 3 | 0.255 | -0.034 | 0.497 | 0.89, 0.98, 0.87 |

**Reading.** On held-out groups the grouped split-conformal intervals cover close to the target (P 0.919; S 0.893); this is a clear change from v2, where intervals calibrated on groups seen in training covered only about 0.64 of the official test set, and it supports the diagnosis that the earlier failure came from calibrating on unrepresentative images. Limits: (i) intervals are wide (mean width about 1.8 on a 0-4 scale); (ii) a constant-width interval from the same model's residuals reaches practically the same coverage at about the same width (P 0.916, S 0.883), so **no benefit of the learned sigma over a constant width is demonstrated**; (iii) sigma correlates positively but unevenly with absolute error (Spearman 0.15-0.42) and low-sigma terciles sometimes under-cover; (iv) per-fold coverage varies from 170/200 to 197/200, as expected from 6-8 calibration groups; (v) held-out groups remain closer to the training data than the official test set, and coverage on the official test set is lower (below).

## 7. Official test set (descriptive, retrospective; never used for any decision)
Mean over the 15 fold-models of each experiment (each model scored on all 300 test images):

| Model | PLCC | SROCC | KROCC | RMSE | MAE | MSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 0.853 | 0.855 | 0.665 | 0.674 | 0.549 | 0.458 |
| B | 0.860 | 0.863 | 0.675 | 0.641 | 0.526 | 0.418 |
| C | 0.849 | 0.850 | 0.659 | 0.696 | 0.573 | 0.497 |

Experiment C intervals (each fold's P quantile): mean coverage 0.756 at mean width 1.82; per-model coverage ranges from 0.52 to 0.96. Coverage is again below 0.90 on content that is further from the training data than the v3 held-out groups, i.e. the exchangeability assumption does not extend to the official test set. The 45 models score the same 300 images, so these are not 45 independent observations.

Differences in training size (about 590 vs 800 vs 900 images), partition type and, for 001/003, BatchNorm epsilon and the 900/100 split, mean no direct comparability is claimed. The ordering v2 validation > v3 held-out groups > official test supports (does not prove) the explanation that image-level splitting inflated v2's validation numbers and that the v3 held-out groups are a harder, more honest, but still easier-than-test estimate. v3 models on the official test (PLCC about 0.85-0.86) are slightly below v2 models (about 0.87), consistent with training on fewer images.

## 9. What study v3 can and cannot establish
**Can:** performance of A, B and C on held-out groups of near-identical images, with calibration fitted on groups unseen in training; that grouped calibration restores near-nominal marginal coverage on held-out groups where the v2 protocol did not; that the v2 null result for the ranking objective is not stable under group-aware evaluation (small, seed-dependent benefit); group-level uncertainty of paired comparisons; that the learned sigma shows no demonstrated advantage over constant-width intervals.
**Cannot:** patient-level generalization (no identifiers); confirmatory evidence (the official test set was examined before); robustness of B's benefit across training seeds (3 seeds, one inconsistent); validity of the intervals for content less similar to training than these groups (the official test set is such a case: coverage below target); any claim of novelty; generalization beyond this dataset. Intervals are group-level and may still be optimistic because groups are not patients.
